text:
Talia Benson: hey all, need 30 mins of alignment on marketplace SKU definitions + naming conventions. also which add-ons are separate line items vs included. goal: single taxonomy across AWS + GCP + Redwood console/billing.

Nikhil Sharma: +1. hosted side is currently a mess: “API credits”, “pro”, “enterprise” floating around. we need marketplace-friendly names that still map cleanly to internal plan codes.

Lauren Bishop: dedicated too. AWS wants clear dimensioning and “what the buyer gets” per product/plan. also add-ons can’t be ambiguous.

Vivek Kulkarni: private: do we treat VPC and on-prem as separate SKUs or a single “Private” SKU w/ deployment option? GCP reviewer hinted they prefer fewer base SKUs.

Soojin Lee: from copy/listing standpoint: fewer SKUs is better, but procurement wants line items for add-ons (compliance, retention, premium SLA). also naming should be consistent + not overpromise.

Naomi Feldman: reminder: avoid bundling compliance claims into base SKU names unless the controls are actually baseline + universally applicable. “Compliance Pack” as add-on is safer.

Talia Benson: ok proposed baseline structure (v2):
1) Redwood Hosted API (usage-based)
2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity)
3) Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem)
Add-ons: Compliance Pack, Extended Log Retention, Premium SLA.
Need to decide: what’s included by default vs paid add-on.

Nikhil Sharma: Hosted API base should include: standard encryption in transit/at rest, basic audit logs (events), 30d log retention (or whatever is current), standard support.

Naomi Feldman: careful: “audit logs” means different things. we can say “administrative/event audit logs available in Console” but not “full audit logging of all customer data access” unless true.

Soojin Lee: copy can say “Audit logging for admin actions and API events” (or similar), and refer to Security FAQ.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated base: dedicated GPU pool + isolation + configurable autoscaling + baseline SLA? We’ve been telling customers Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime.

Markus Klein: field expectation: Dedicated comes with an SLA option but not always default. Some want premium response times.

Cole Summers: from billing: easiest if SLA is always an entitlement (even if included). then premium is an additional entitlement. but marketplace line items matter.

Nadia Rahman: metering: Hosted is token-based meter. Dedicated is monthly commit meter + overage (if any). Private is annual license + support tier. add-ons should be binary entitlements, not usage meters, if possible.

Vivek Kulkarni: Private base should include SSO/SAML + SCIM? or are those “enterprise” features we want gated via add-on?

Naomi Feldman: SSO/SCIM is often expected for Private. I’d avoid making “SSO Pack” a marketplace add-on; reviewers and buyers may see it as table stakes.

Soojin Lee: agree. also “Private” buyer persona is regulated / enterprise; they’ll balk if SSO is an add-on. better to include it in Private base.

Talia Benson: let’s pin decisions:
- Hosted API base includes: API access, model catalog, standard support, basic admin/API event logs.
- Dedicated base includes: dedicated capacity + baseline SLA (uptime only) + standard support.
- Private base includes: private control plane + customer-managed networking + SSO/SAML (+SCIM?) + audit logs.
Open question: are “Compliance Pack” and “Extended Retention” add-ons for ALL three, or only Dedicated/Private?

Nikhil Sharma: Hosted customers do ask for longer retention and compliance paperwork. I think add-ons should be available across all deployment modes (even if implementation differs). at least on marketplace, they want a line item.

Naomi Feldman: compliance: we can offer a “Compliance Pack” add-on across modes, but language should be “access to compliance documentation / audit reports under NDA” + “enhanced controls” only if those controls actually toggle.

Cole Summers: for implementation: Compliance Pack is mostly sales motion + gating access to evidence portal. Retention is a product knob (log retention days). Premium SLA is a support contract knob.

Lauren Bishop: for Dedicated, log retention longer than 30d matters for audits; should be add-on. For Hosted, retention is trickier bc it’s multi-tenant.

Nadia Rahman: on Hosted: we can still do “extended retention of request/response metadata and operational logs” vs “prompt/response content” retention (which is sensitive). we should be explicit what’s retained.

Soojin Lee: +1. listing FAQ can say: default retention X days; Extended Retention increases retention of operational logs; content retention depends on customer settings.

Vivek Kulkarni: naming convention question: do we keep “Redwood Hosted API” or “Redwood Inference API”? customers search “inference”.

Soojin Lee: I prefer “Redwood Inference (Hosted API)” as the product name, but AWS/GCP have character limits. maybe:
- “Redwood Inference – Hosted API”
- “Redwood Inference – Dedicated”
- “Redwood Inference – Private”
Then plan within product: “Pay-as-you-go” vs “Committed Spend” etc.

Talia Benson: +1 on “Redwood Inference – X” for marketplace. internal billing can keep “hosted_api”, “dedicated”, “private”.

Nikhil Sharma: Hosted plans inside AWS: we likely need 2: PayGo and Committed Spend (annual commit but billed via marketplace). Otherwise procurement can’t do committed.

Cole Summers: yes, two Hosted SKUs helps: 
- hosted_api_payg
- hosted_api_commit
They map to same meter but commit sets minimum monthly.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated: do we split by GPU type/size? AWS wants product dimensions; but we can sell “Dedicated Capacity Unit” and then allocate hardware behind the scenes.

Nadia Rahman: if we hide GPU type, pricing becomes harder to justify. but if we expose it, SKU explosion.

Markus Klein: field reality: buyers want “H100 pool” vs “L40S pool” sometimes. for marketplace procurement they mainly care about committed spend + region + isolation, less exact GPU model.

Vivek Kulkarni: can we do “Dedicated – Standard” and “Dedicated – Performance” tiers, where “Performance” implies newer GPUs, without naming specific chips?

Naomi Feldman: careful with implicit promises. if “Performance” is just higher throughput SLO, ok. don’t imply specific hardware unless guaranteed.

Soojin Lee: messaging-wise: “Dedicated – Standard” and “Dedicated – Premium” might read like support tiers. I’d rather call it “Dedicated Capacity” with selectable configuration during onboarding.

Talia Benson: I think we keep Dedicated as one base SKU per cloud (AWS/GCP) and configure pool size in-console. For marketplace, pricing dimension can be “Capacity Units” (CU) per month.

Cole Summers: that’s compatible with billing. CU maps to internal “dedicated_capacity_unit” meter. actual hardware allocation stays internal.

Lauren Bishop: ok but we need guardrails: CU corresponds to target throughput / tokens/sec band.

Nikhil Sharma: back to add-ons: I propose 3 add-ons as separate line items for all base products:
A) Compliance Pack
B) Extended Log Retention (365d)
C) Premium SLA (24x7 + faster response)

Naomi Feldman: +1, with Compliance Pack definition: “access to compliance documentation and security review support”. also disclaimer: availability varies by region/deployment mode.

Soojin Lee: and “Premium SLA” should not be offered on Hosted PayGo self-serve without sales involvement? we’ve historically limited premium support.

Markus Klein: yes. in practice: Premium SLA is enterprise-only. but marketplace buyers may still purchase it; we should allow but route onboarding to sales/CS.

Talia Benson: so rule: Premium SLA add-on is purchasable but requires activation by Redwood (entitlement -> CS ack). docs should set expectation.

Cole Summers: that means entitlement state: “pending activation” until support team flips.

Nadia Rahman: make sure metering doesn’t start for Premium SLA until activated, or we’ll have disputes.

Vivek Kulkarni: Private SKU question: do we split “Private – VPC” vs “Private – On-Prem”? Or keep “Private” and ask during onboarding?

Talia Benson: for marketplace review, I’d keep one “Private” product, plan “Private Deployment License” and onboarding step chooses VPC vs on-prem. less SKU churn.

Soojin Lee: ok but listing needs to be explicit: “Deploy in your VPC (AWS/GCP) or on-prem with Redwood Private package.”

Naomi Feldman: plus shared responsibility language.

Talia Benson: summarizing decisions (unless objections):
- Marketplace product family naming: “Redwood Inference – Hosted API / Dedicated / Private”
- Hosted plans: Pay-as-you-go + Committed Spend (2 SKUs)
- Dedicated: one SKU (Capacity Units / month)
- Private: one SKU (License)
- Add-ons as separate line items across all three: Compliance Pack, Extended Log Retention (365d), Premium SLA (activation required)
- Private base includes SSO/SAML (+SCIM if already shipped) and standard audit/event logs.

Nikhil Sharma: sounds good. action: I’ll update Hosted SKU descriptions + internal plan codes mapping.

Lauren Bishop: I’ll draft the Dedicated CU definition + what’s included vs add-on (esp SLA language).

Vivek Kulkarni: I’ll confirm Private includes SCIM today; if not, we’ll only claim SSO/SAML in base.

Naomi Feldman: I’ll provide approved wording for Compliance Pack + retention disclaimers.

Soojin Lee: I’ll incorporate naming convention into messaging framework + listing copy blocks.

Cole Summers: I’ll sanity check entitlement model: base sku entitlements + add-on entitlements + “pending activation” state for premium SLA.

Talia Benson: perfect. I’ll capture this in the SKU catalog doc and link here once updated.

Evelyn Hart: +1 to keeping SKU set minimal. please ensure “Committed Spend” isn’t confusing with “Reserved capacity” (Dedicated). clarity matters.

Soojin Lee: noted. maybe “Hosted API – Commit” vs “Dedicated – Reserved Capacity” in the UI.

Talia Benson: cool. closing thread unless new concerns.
